At 5:15 every weekday morning, the 22 bus picks up exactly four people at my stop. I know their names now, though it took most of a year.

Mr. Okafor reads the same paperback he's been reading since September. Dana sleeps. The woman I call the Captain (she wears a navy peacoat, and I've never been brave enough to ask her real name) does a crossword in pen.

I started riding the 22 because swim practice begins at 6. I kept noticing it because it's the only forty minutes of my day when nobody expects anything from me. No splits, no grades, no group chat.

What I've done with that time is small. I learned 300 words of Portuguese from an app. I wrote, by hand, a letter to my aunt. I finished one-third of a crossword and was corrected, kindly, in pen.

If you ask what I'll bring to a campus, it's partly this: I'm good at being a regular somewhere.
